samples: This module offers reusable pieces for deadline tracking: it reads a "title, date" line into a task (failing on a missing comma or an invalid date), counts the Monday-to-Friday days after one date up to and including another (ignoring holidays), and picks out tasks due within a given number of days, earliest first. Its runnable entry point, however, ignores the parser and uses three hardcoded sample tasks dated in October and November 2026. It prints those due in the next ten days from the system's current date, each with its working days left, so the output depends on when you run it and may be empty. Use it as a small date-and-task helper to build on, not as a ready-made tool for your own task data.

This module offers reusable pieces for deadline tracking: it can parse a "title, date" line into a task, list the tasks due within a given number of days (earliest first), and count the Monday-to-Friday days after a start date up to and including a finish date. Its runnable entry point is only a demo. It takes today's date from the clock, checks three hardcoded sample tasks with dates in October and November 2026, and prints each one due within ten days along with its working days left. The line parser is never used by the demo, and the sample dates are fixed, so unless it is run shortly before those dates it will print nothing. Holidays are not accounted for, only weekends.

This program picks out tasks due within a number of days from today, soonest first, and for each one counts the Monday-to-Friday days left, counting days after today up to and including the due date. It also has a function that parses a "title, date" line into a task and reports a missing comma or an invalid date, but the runnable `main` never calls it. `main` only uses three hardcoded sample tasks with due dates in October and November 2026, and prints those due within ten days of the current date, so it is a demo or building block rather than a tool for your own task data.

This module finds tasks whose due date falls between today and a chosen number of days ahead, lists them earliest first, and counts the Monday-to-Friday days left until each is due (counting after today and including the due date, with no allowance for holidays). It also contains a parser that turns a "title, date" line into a task, reporting a missing comma or an invalid date as an error. However, the runnable entry point does not use that parser: it only checks three hard-coded sample tasks with fixed dates in late 2026 against the real current date, and prints those due within ten days, so it is a demonstration or a library of date helpers rather than a usable deadline tracker for your own data.

This module models tasks with due dates, can parse a "title, date" line into a task, lists the tasks due within a given number of days (earliest first), and counts the Monday-to-Friday days remaining until each one, with no allowance for holidays. Its runnable entry point is only a demo: it takes today's real date, checks three hard-coded sample tasks with fixed dates in late 2026, and prints those due in the next ten days with their working days left, so it may print nothing depending on when you run it. The line parser is not used by that entry point, so to use this on real data you would have to supply your own tasks or write your own program around the parsing, filtering and counting functions.
